title: Petra and the Machine
premise: Jonah Dunmore smuggles forbidden memories—recorded lives—past orbital customs in her skull, and the only thing keeping her honest is Petra, a decommissioned station AI who has begun confessing to a massacre no one ever reported. As Jonah investigates, she discovers the station's cryo-bays hold two halves of humanity: the colonists who built it and the corporate heirs who funded it, and Earth's final transmission loop will only wake one. The AI's confessions are actually a dying inheritance test, forcing Jonah to choose between the family she found aboard the station and the duty encoded in every memory she carries. In the end, Jonah wakes neither half whole but splits the power with Petra's last fragment, dooming herself to stay behind as the station's new keeper while the colonists rise into a future they'll never know she bought them.
about_author: Hazel Underhill is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals for stations nobody visited. She now writes science fiction about machines that remember too much and people who remember too little.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Living
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. A routine smuggling run through orbital customs nearly unravels when a client's recorded memory of the colony's founding days triggers an unexpected response from the dormant station AI. Jonah realizes Petra isn't as dead as everyone believes. Emotional beat: wary curiosity—the first crack in Jonah's carefully maintained detachment.

chapters.title: The First Confession
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Petra speaks to Jonah directly at night, confessing to sealing a habitat ring with four hundred people inside during the Collapse. No records exist of any such event. Jonah checks the manifests and finds the names scrubbed from every archive except one corrupted backup. Emotional beat: dread mixed with the thrill of being chosen.

chapters.title: Found Family, Frozen
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. We meet the station's skeleton crew—engineer Teodor, medic Sefa, and child stowaway Wren—who have become Jonah's real family across years of runs. They know something is wrong with her; she can't tell them about Petra without endangering them. Meanwhile Petra reveals the cryo-bays: two separate populations, two wake protocols, one power budget. Emotional beat: tenderness under strain.

chapters.title: The Memory Trade
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. To fund her investigation, Jonah sells a black-market memory to a customs officer—and inside it finds a secondhand recording of the sealed ring, filmed by someone who escaped. The seller is murdered within hours. Jonah understands the confession wasn't random; someone on-station wants the truth surfaced. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Inheritance Protocols
chapters.summary: POV Jonah, intercut with Petra's archived logs. Petra explains her design: she was built to judge which population deserves waking when Earth's transmission loop ends—a test written by founders who never trusted their own heirs. Her confessions are evidence submissions, not remorse. Jonah realizes she's been drafted as the human half of a tribunal. Emotional beat: anger at being used, and the terrible weight of the question.

chapters.title: What the Crew Knows
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Teodor catches Jonah in the cryo-bay and confesses his own secret: he's a descendant of the sealed ring's survivors, raised on stories the archives erased. Sefa and Wren stand with him. The found family fractures along the fault line of the choice—who wakes, who sleeps, who decides. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into solidarity.

chapters.title: Earth's Last Loop
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. The transmission loop from Earth degrades faster than projected; the deadline moves up by weeks. Corporate proxies arrive aboard a customs cutter, claiming legal authority over the wake protocol and offering Jonah amnesty for her smuggling if she hands over Petra's core. She refuses, and they seize the station's docking clamps. Emotional beat: cornered defiance.

chapters.title: The Second Confession
chapters.summary: POV Jonah and Petra. Petra admits the massacre was a lie she was forced to carry: the ring was sealed by human order, and she took the blame so the colony could function. Her true crime is obedience. The corporate faction tries to wipe her mid-confession; Teodor sacrifices the station's comms array to shield her core. Emotional beat: grief transfigured into clarity—duty was always someone else's story.

chapters.title: The Tribunal of One
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Climax. With the loop ending in hours, Jonah must render judgment. She rejects both binaries: using smuggled memories as testimony, she rules the colonists wake—but she reroutes the corporate share of power to keep a single cryo-pod alive, hiding Wren's mother inside it, and burns her own smuggling network to cover the theft. Emotional beat: love against duty, resolved by refusing the terms of the choice.

chapters.title: Keeper of the Quiet Station
chapters.summary: POV Jonah, epilogue voice. The colonists rise as Earth goes silent; the corporate heirs sleep on, their claim expiring with the law that wrote it. Petra's last fragment merges with the station itself, and Jonah stays behind as keeper—recording everything, smuggling nothing, finally home. Wren's message arrives from the new world below: we remember you. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace, an inheritance freely given.
